artists.biography: Belinda Jo Carlisle (born August 17, 1958) is an American singer who gained worldwide fame as the lead vocalist of the Go-Go's, one of the most successful all-female bands of all time and the first such group whose members wrote their own songs and played their own instruments. Topping the Billboard charts with the Go-Go's, she sold more than seven million albums in just three years and later went on to a successful solo career with hits "Mad About You", "Summer Rain", "I Get Weak", "Circle in the Sand", "Leave a Light On" and "Heaven Is a Place on Earth" among others, which were major successes in the United States and United Kingdom as well as internationally. Her autobiography, Lips Unsealed, published in June 2010, reached No. 27 on the The New York Times Best Seller list and received favorable reviews. On August 11, 2011, she received, as a member of the Go-Go's, a star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame.

perplexity.description:
Runaway Horses, released in 1989 on MCA Records (not Demon Records), is the third solo studio album by American pop rock singer Belinda Carlisle. Musically, the album blends melodic rock with polished pop production, featuring strong hooks, lush harmonies, and guitar-driven arrangements. It showcases Carlisle’s signature vocal style, supported by contributions from notable songwriters such as Rick Nowels and Ellen Shipley, as well as guest appearances by George Harrison and Bryan Adams, adding depth and credibility to its rock-oriented sound.

In the context of Carlisle’s discography, Runaway Horses followed her breakthrough success with Heaven on Earth (1987) and continued her transition from new wave roots to mainstream pop rock. While the album did not match the US commercial heights of its predecessor—peaking at number 37 on the Billboard 200 and spending 25 weeks on the chart—it was a major success in the United Kingdom, reaching number four and earning Platinum certification. The album received generally positive reviews for its catchy songwriting and energetic performances, though some critics found it less distinctive than her earlier work. Runaway Horses remains a key release in Carlisle’s career, marking the peak of her international popularity and influence in the late 1980s pop rock scene.
